reviews.text: [quote][b][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset_flip]Warning: Asset Flip![/url][/b] Stickman Killing Zombie is a Digital Homicide style asset flip, or what Valve calls a "Fake Game". The "developer" paid for/pirated a few Unity asset store packs, dumped them all in a blender, and submitted it to Valve as if they're real game developers.[/quote] Two notable criteria for what makes an asset flip instead of legitimate use of stock assets are whether those assets comprise the majority of the game, and whether the "developer" properly credited the people who created most of the assets in the game. This game fails both of those tests. The "developers" here didn't credit any of the artists and real, actual game developers who created the assets here, so this is plagiarism, as well as cash grab shovelware. In this case, the asset flipper took a basic Unity blueprint for making a brawler and populated it with lazy stickmen assets and a few assets from Synty like the "Simple Apocalypse" pack, to make a minimum viable product cash grab. It has no value or merit as a real game. Taking this shovelware seriously as if it was a genuine attempt to make a game, it doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard. There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks. There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display. There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision. The game features lazy minimalist/untextured low-polygon "retro" assets and visuals, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s. The lack of textures is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with. It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the game. It looks bad as a result of their decisions, and that's just another reason to avoid it. Bewilderingly, the game doesn't include proper audio controls, so you can't turn off the annoying sound/background music, you'll need to alt+tab out and stop it using the Windows sound mixer. This is obviously not okay and it's unclear why the developers chose not to include this basic feature. The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts. PC gamers will be insulted by the presence of console peasant children's toy controller prompts, despite this being on PC. Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for. These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game. The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it. At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the game all-time peak player count was only ONE player. That's right, only one person ever played this at a time. When I played this for the purposes of reviewing it, I equalled the peak player count for the game. OUCH. The only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it. Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected. The game contains stock/store assets/libraries/packages, but the "developer" here hasn't credited the people who actually did the work for the game. In some cases this breaches the license agreement the developer signed for the use of those assets. Worse, some of the assets are licensed under a [b]NON-COMMERCIAL AGREEMENT[/b], but the developer is violating those licenses [b]FOR PROFIT[/b]. This is not just a contractual/license breach, in many jurisdictions this is a breach of criminal law. Claiming credit for the work of others as well as breaching software licenses and breaking the law is highly unethical. This kind of asset flipping isn't harmless. It makes it harder for gamers to find genuinely made games from ethical developers. It makes it harder for genuine indie developers, who put hard work into trying to make real games, to find an audience for their products. It gives indie developers a bad name. So, should you buy this game? Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam? Stickman Killing Zombie is relatively cheap at $3 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend. Remember that if you buy a game from an unethical developer, you're putting your money at risk.

Stickman Killing Zombie, developed by Yurii Nikshych and published by GrabTheGames, presents itself as a stripped-down, arcade-style action game that thrives on immediacy rather than complexity. It throws players into a stylized, zombie-infested setting where a lone stickman warrior cuts through hordes using a vivid red blade, delivering a gameplay loop that is easy to grasp from the very first moment. There is no heavy onboarding, no intricate systems to learn—just movement, attacks, and survival. This simplicity is both its defining strength and its most noticeable limitation, shaping the entire experience into something intentionally lightweight and accessible. The combat system is built around responsiveness and repetition, offering a satisfying rhythm of slashing through enemies and watching them collapse under exaggerated ragdoll physics. Hits feel impactful in a visual sense, with enemies flying or crumpling in ways that reinforce the game’s arcade sensibilities. While the mechanics are basic, there is a certain hypnotic quality to the flow of combat, especially in shorter play sessions. It becomes the kind of game you can pick up without much thought, play for a while, and put down without feeling like you’ve left anything unfinished. However, this same straightforward design also means that combat lacks depth; there are no meaningful upgrades, skill variations, or evolving strategies to keep players engaged over longer stretches. Visually, the game leans into its minimalist identity with simple stickman models placed within modest 3D environments. The aesthetic is clean and functional rather than impressive, and while it maintains clarity during gameplay, it does little to build atmosphere or immersion. The environments themselves feel repetitive, offering limited variation and little sense of progression as players move from one area to another. The zombie theme, while fitting for the gameplay, is not explored in any narrative or environmental storytelling capacity, leaving the world feeling static and purely utilitarian. Progression is structured around missions that can be approached in a relatively flexible order, but these objectives rarely deviate from straightforward combat tasks. Whether it’s clearing out waves of enemies or surviving encounters, the core activities remain largely unchanged from beginning to end. Enemy types do not evolve significantly, and the absence of new mechanics or challenges makes the experience feel predictable fairly quickly. The game’s short overall length reinforces this, as it can be completed in just a few hours, making it clear that it is designed for quick consumption rather than long-term investment. Despite its limitations, the game manages to succeed in delivering short bursts of entertainment. Its pacing works in its favor, never dragging things out or overstaying its welcome. The low barrier to entry—both in terms of difficulty and cost—makes it an easy recommendation for players looking for something casual and undemanding. It’s the kind of title that fits neatly into a gap between larger, more demanding games, offering a brief distraction rather than a fully immersive experience. Ultimately, Stickman Killing Zombie feels like a modest project that accomplishes exactly what it sets out to do, even if it doesn’t aim particularly high. It provides a simple, accessible hack-and-slash loop that can be enjoyable in small doses, but it lacks the depth, variety, and ambition needed to stand out in a crowded genre. Players who appreciate straightforward, no-frills action may find it worthwhile for a short time, while those seeking more engaging systems or lasting replay value will likely move on quickly. Rating: 6/10

游戏内无教程无设置。wasd/↑←↓→键移动鼠标左键攻击esc退出。 一共四个区域，每个区域30个任务，解锁下个区域需完成指定数量任务，游戏玩法：操作黑色火柴人一直杀杀杀+跑跑跑，完成目标任务解锁撤离点，相近的三个任务可以在单个关卡？共同完成。部分任务可以逃课一直跑跑跑，敌方追不上消失在视野里后就再也不会追上来了，有金光的金色和红色小人是范围伤害需要立马杀掉，不然就是你在前面跑，他们追在后面哐哐燃烧你的血量。 人物走不了回头路，想往回走？很遗憾那里已经形成一面空气墙了。 人物可升级，大概是每个部位升两次就能通关了，但是升级所需金币设置不合理，第四个区域每关地上隔不了多远就是成堆的金币，前面几个区域需要跑很远很远才能看到两三堆金币。 到第四个区域发现敌方可以被场景内尖锐建筑物刺死。 不要一直停留在一个地方杀杀杀，敌方尸体有建模，堆太多就走不了只能困死在尸体堆看着撤离提示闪烁。 个人不太喜欢这个游戏的视角，当人物跑到屏幕上方就看不到场景下方的任何东西。 通关即全成就，成就有延迟，需要在关闭游戏后才会弹解锁。 在第四个区域完成楼层最顶上三个任务的任意一个后会有一个动画。 2026/4/21

It is exactly what it sounds like and honestly, that’s kind of the whole appeal. You jump in, start smashing through waves of zombies, and it doesn’t really try to be anything more than that. It’s simple, a bit janky at times, but completely straightforward. Combat is pretty basic, mostly just swinging a sword and clearing out enemies. It’s very mindless, you’re not really thinking, just reacting. Don’t expect tight mechanics or anything super polished though, it definitely feels rough around the edges. Visually it’s as minimal as it gets. Stick figures, plain environments, nothing fancy, but it works for the kind of game it is. The focus is clearly on just throwing you into the action without any distractions. It’s not something you’ll remember for its depth or design, but as a quick way to kill time, it does the job. Pretty repetitive overall, but fine in short bursts.

I wouldn't pay for this. I will say it works, more or less. I try to scale my reviews to the expectations of the game to begin with, and you more or less know what's going on in the gameplay above. This is the game of all time, so I'm going to waste my life explaining why this review is negative even though you know for damn sure you're not actually buying this for anything other than a bet. WASD and mouse clicks or the spacebar if you have a trackpad and don't want it to tilt. That's basically it. There's no strategy to most of the missions, you just spam swings regardless of the animation on sccreen and you'll land hits. I'll start with that, then: enemy variations are lazy and trite, without meaningfully affecting gameplay when they do seem interesting besides being much more than hit sponges towards the end. Animations are misleading, as bite and hit movements don't reflect the damage dealt or received and are in fact way out of sync. Mere contact is enough. Weapon upgrades don't feel like they change anything. Sound design is pathetic. I have strong doubts that the one publishing this game composed it themselves. It's still one-note and it's not interesting. It's not a selling point to have more interesting audio replace your own. The balancing is downright malicious, too. The music is quiet, as are enemy sounds and weapon swings. Explosions and fence hits are deafening in comparison, and if you've sensitive ears like myself you have to wonder if the one publishing this was van Gogh in the tail end of his life. It looks... like an application. All the models are lazy. I get there's an appeal for pared-back, basic games, some of those are my favourites. This is lame by comparison. I've seen more inventive stuff on Friv. In 2015. Or Wii shovelware (some of which was genuinely enjoyable). Missions can be cheesed. The only one worth any tsrategy is health missions, for which you just zig-zag a bit more. Otherwise you're fine to run through waves, to complete 3 missions at a time. To 'win' the 'game' you need only complete the top right missions in 'space'. You can do this before completing that tier. Try a little harder. --- [u]Technical stuff:[/u] Played on Linux Mint 22.3. Be surprised this game even walks. It runs fine, there's a native Linux version which I used but save data won't carry over between a native Linux build and a Proton version. Bonus points for even having one, though, for what little effort was expended on making this thing exist it's still more than base game Assetto Corsa on PC.

I think picking this up at a 100% discount counts as free? I'll be honest, the only reason I even launched this game is because it looked like a short game that has easy to obtain achievements that actually count towards my completion percentage. Nothing against the style of game, it's not my type of game. Close, but off the mark for me. Honestly with some tweaking I could say this is a decent game, however as it is I can't. -The attacks don't seem to make sense, I have no idea how to tell if I'm hitting the enemy or not. -I have no idea how to determine how far away from the enemies I need to be in order to avoid being attacked -The controls are poor and I have no idea how to tell what buttons do what. The only thing I know is the person who made this game based it off of a nintendo controller -I don't understand the upgrade weapons/armor system. Does the weapon do more damage when you upgrade it? I can't tell. Also, Why does the weapon upgrade to lvl 100, and some of the armor upgrades to lvl 80 while the rest upgrade to lvl 60? It bothers me each of there max levels is different. -I experenced getting stuck in levels several times. Moving down to the bottom of the screen to pick up gold but getting stuck because there is debres infront of me and the screen doesn't allow you to move backwards once the screen has moved over. -I cannot explain, nor understand why sometimes I can complete several other objects/missions while completing certain missions. If I kill 50 zombies it will sometimes complete the mission that says to kill 15 zombies, but not always. -the last zone after I "saved the world" even though I didn't complete all missions in the area, almost every mission that was not completed in that zone (but not all) caused me to watch the same world saving cut scene. Overall I think the game is missing polish. Clean up the controls and combat a bit, give a little explaination for controls, make sure the features you've added are working correctly. I'm not expecting triple A title quality, but I do believe this game could be drastically improved with a little more time and effort.

Before you buy - Stickman Killing Zombie - In this review, I will evaluate different aspects of the game, such as the gameplay, content and achievements. I will try to be as in depth as possible, while avoiding any kind of spoilers. The review will end with a conclusion, as with all of my reviews, which will state whether or not it is worth its price. Of course, this is only my opinion, and by definition of an opinion, is personal to my own experience with the game. [SKIP TO THE END OF THE REVIEW FOR THE SUMMARY] Art and Graphics - The art style of this game feels very much like what you would see out of a niche mobile game. It is playable at most and downright low effort at worst. It kind of feels like an asset flip, as not all of the game's models seem to fit into the same art style. Some enemies and items feel as if they have been ripped from another art-style and forced into this game. Gameplay - The gameplay would be alright, if it worked. The premise of killing large groups of zombies on a scrolling map is not bad, and may appeal to some users, but the game has an annoying amount of problems, and borders on an unenjoyable experience. There are multiple ways to be softlocked in the levels. For some reason, dead enemies actually have collision, and can entirely stop you from progressing any further. In some levels, the actual finishing portal just does not spawn at all. The map has obstacles such as vehicles positioned randomly, and only scrolls one way. You can not go backwards. It should be obvious that this is a bad idea, as you can become permanently stuck due to bad generation. The *singular* attack in the entire game has no cooldown, and can be autoclicked to cheesed the *entire* game. Story and Length - I will not say much here as there is very little, if not nothing to talk about. You move from named area to named area, killing enemies and completing fetch quests. That is basically it. The missions are all entirely composed of the same tasks, all the way up to the end of the game, which has no special or interesting feature. The enemies do change as you progress though, which is interesting I suppose? It is not a very long game either, and should not take long to beat. Achievements - This game is extremely easy to perfect. The achievements are tied to overall progression. Since that itself is quick and easy, so are the achievements. Performance - I think it's rather obvious that it runs well. I mean.. it's a very simply graphically styled game about a stickman. It is never going to be difficult to run. Conclusion - Art and Graphics - [OK] Gameplay - [AWFUL] Story - [LACKING] Length - [LACKING] Achievements - [EASY] Performance - [AMAZING] Is it worth the price - Normally I would go into depth here, but the simple answer is no. If the game worked, it may be a yes. For £2.49, you're paying for a game that barely even functions. Do not waste any money on this game. If I had not received it for free, I would not be writing this review. [Feel free to leave your opinions in the replies! I'm interested to hear what everybody else thought of it.]

Stickman Killing Zombie is a zombie apocalypse game with a production budget the size of a canteen's lunch money. There are no elite soldiers, no advanced technology, just a simple stickman who decides the best way to save the world is to punch everything that moves. The gameplay is simple, easy to pick up, and perfect for killing time without having to think too hard. There's not much variety or depth, so after a while it feels like working overtime at the office, doing the same job, just in a different location. Stickman Killing Zombie is fun enough for a quick diversion. Sometimes, the best solution to facing thousands of zombies is to be more stubborn than the zombies themselves.

[h2]The zombies are green zombies? No wait... Uhh... might as well be army soldiers.[/h2] I started playing this out of curiosity and then my cat died. So there's that. Yea, so this indie game is kind of like a lazy alpha with assets that look like they have no texture maps whatsoever. The gameplay is just hack and slash. It's alright, I guess. You get little missions where you kill army dudes (err... I mean zombies), collect gold, save kittens, repair turrets that then shoot you down, fight the occasional boss, and rinse and repeat. The music is absolutely nonexistent... Mainly because I muted it. Just a heads up: you can sometimes complete multiple mission objectives at once if they overlap, but it's inconsistent and doesn't always work. Bug maybe. I don't care to finish this game. I have no time for these shenanigans. Time to go play the rest of my backlog. [h2]5/10[/h2] [h3][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45905648-Gork%2527s-Game-Grind/]Check out my curated list of games[/url][/h3]
